HatchPattern__ScreedAndRender__Meta.Meta__Description: Screed, render and plaster - an even stipple of dots. In section it fills a screed or a render coat; on an elevation, drawn light, it is the usual tone for a rendered wall.
HatchPattern__ScreedAndRender__Meta.Meta__WhyPaperUnits: Every length here is PAPER millimetres, like the dash patterns in Na__LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Config__.json, so the hatch measures the same on the sheet at 1:20 and at 1:100. Pattern scale adjusts from there.
HatchPattern__ScreedAndRender__Meta.Meta__WhyScatter: The positions are a blue-noise scatter, generated ONCE and written in below as fixed numbers, so screen and paper can never disagree. It was scored on a torus - the gap across a tile seam counts like any other gap - and against the regularities that survive a repeat: two marks sharing a column (an endless vertical line once the tile repeats) or a row. A lattice was never an option: it lays visible stripes across a wall.
HatchPattern__ScreedAndRender__Meta.Meta__WhyInsideTheTile: Every mark sits wholly inside the tile, so nothing crosses a seam at all: a browser clips a <pattern> at its tile edge and the PDF stamper does not.
HatchPattern__ScreedAndRender__Meta.Meta__DotSize: A dot is as wide as the line weight: 0.70 pt (0.25 mm) as standard. Pattern line pt makes the stipple heavier or finer without moving a dot.

HatchPattern__ScreedAndRender__Identity.Identity__Description: How this pattern is named, found and grouped in the pattern lists.
HatchPattern__ScreedAndRender__Identity.Identity__Note: Sand and cement work: screeds, renders, plaster, mortar beds, sand blinding.

HatchPattern__ScreedAndRender__Tile.Tile__Description: The repeating cell, in paper millimetres.
HatchPattern__ScreedAndRender__Tile.Tile__Note: Forty-four dots: one to every 5.8 square millimetres.

HatchPattern__ScreedAndRender__Defaults.Defaults__Description: What the pattern draws with until a use sets its own. The stroke is 0.70 pt (0.2469 mm) at scale 1 and grows with the pattern scale; a line weight typed in the panel does not. 'inherit' takes the colour of whatever carries the hatch - a vector's edge colour - until a pattern colour is picked.

HatchPattern__ScreedAndRender__Glyphs.Glyphs__Description: Drawn about the glyph's own origin, y pointing DOWN, in tile millimetres. Strokes only: the PDF stamps a tile as lines and never fills one.

Dot.Glyph__Note: A tenth of a millimetre of line: with round caps it prints as a dot the width of the line weight.

HatchPattern__ScreedAndRender__Bounds.Bounds__Description: How far a use may scale and turn this pattern before it stops reading as the material.
